entries.test: Compare the biography's errors and omissions with Harry Shearer's Wikipedia page as it appeared when the post was published.
entries.note: The source says almost all the information was readily available; the proposition drops that qualification.

entries.test: Published controlled studies could establish whether humanlike LLM language causes users to attribute humanlike processes to the systems.
entries.note: This asserts a causal effect on users, which can be studied publicly.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and technical evaluations could show whether LLMs ever verify factual assertions against evidence and correct their outputs accordingly.
entries.note: The categorical 'ever' makes demonstrated fact-checking relevant counterevidence.

entries.test: Representative factual benchmarks could measure whether LLMs regularly produce both correct answers and factual errors.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives reliability a plain meaning: factual accuracy.

entries.test: Public model analyses and controlled interventions on learned word associations could test whether those associations cause the false 'British actor' attribution.
entries.note: The proposition broadens a particular mechanism and example into a general account of hallucinations, and specifies embedding space more precisely than the source.

entries.test: Comparable published hallucination evaluations of o3 and earlier OpenAI models would establish whether o3 has higher hallucination rates than some predecessors.
entries.note: 'Not going away' describes persistence in the context of the current model comparison.

entries.test: Published citation-generation experiments and model analyses could test whether structural imitation without source verification produces fabricated references and legal cases.
entries.note: The passage explicitly links fabricated citations to the preceding mechanism.
Calling the performance 'pathetic' is a judgment of worth. The reported benchmark rate is separately checkable.

entries.test: Public spending estimates and evaluations of LLM fact-checking against Wikipedia and supplied CNN articles could assess the cost and reliability assertions.
entries.note: The proposition extracts factual assertions that Marcus endorses within an evaluative sentence.
'May never' expresses a possibility rather than a firm prediction.
The proposition drops the qualification tying 'world model' to particular researchers' usage. Without an agreed definition, readers could reach different answers about that component.

entries.test: Public training-data documentation and factual evaluations against contemporaneous Wikipedia pages could establish whether models trained on Wikipedia regularly contradict it.
entries.note: The proposition captures the asserted failure to adhere reliably to Wikipedia.

entries.test: Published chess legality evaluations and controlled studies of model representations could test both recurring rule violations and their attribution to inadequate rule abstraction.
entries.note: The proposition includes an explicit causal explanation, not just a performance observation.
Coding assistance can be evaluated, but the compound claim supplies no shared criterion for 'human-like computation' or the asserted implication.
'A grasp of reality' has no agreed test here. The spending and elapsed-time components are independently checkable.

entries.test: Public fact-checking evaluations and controlled interventions on models' representations could test the asserted inability and its proposed cause.
entries.note: The sentence attributes an inability to fact-check to superficial understanding; demonstrated fact-checking would challenge its categorical consequence.
This is a recommendation against concentrating AI development exclusively on LLMs.

entries.test: The emergence of a successor AI approach demonstrating reliably better factual accuracy and source verification than the LLMs discussed would establish the predicted improvement.
entries.note: The context supplies a plain reading of 'better' through factual reliability. 'Eventually' sets no deadline.
